description_short: For each etched material in the thermal ALE overview (Table III), list the distinct Reactant 1–3 tuples and count how many entries report each tuple.

paper.title: Thermal atomic layer etching: A review

tables_modeled.label: Table III
tables_modeled.description: Summary of thermal atomic layer etching (ALE) chemistries, including etched material and up to three reactants involved in the thermal ALE cycle.

properties_used.label: material etched
properties_used.role: Identifies the solid being etched in a given thermal ALE chemistry (e.g., SiO2, Al2O3, Si3N4).

properties_used.label: reactant 1
properties_used.role: First reactant used in the thermal ALE sequence (often the initial surface-modifying or ligand-exchange species).

properties_used.label: reactant 2
properties_used.role: Second reactant in the thermal ALE sequence (e.g., counter-reactant for ligand exchange or volatile product formation).

properties_used.label: reactant 3
properties_used.role: Optional third reactant or treatment step used in some thermal ALE chemistries.

aggregation_logic.description: The query groups contributions by material and by the ordered triple (Reactant 1, Reactant 2, Reactant 3) and counts how many table rows share that same combination.
details: Each contribution corresponds to one line in the modeled Table III.
Labels are used where available; otherwise, the raw resource identifiers are used.
The count ?n_reports indicates how often a given material–reactant tuple appears in the table.

output_shape.description: One row per unique material–reactant tuple, with a frequency count.
columns: material: name or label of the etched material.
reactant_1: label or identifier of Reactant 1.
reactant_2: label or identifier of Reactant 2 (may be empty).
reactant_3: label or identifier of Reactant 3 (may be empty).
n_reports: number of contributions reporting that exact tuple.

postprocessing_notes.interpretation: The resulting table can be used to see which thermal ALE chemistries (in terms of reactant combinations) have been studied repeatedly for a given material and which are reported only once, providing a simple empirical indicator of how well-explored different parts of the thermal ALE chemical space are.
